subject: high heels
title: What If You Always Wore High Heels?

scenes.text: What if you wore high heels every day? Flat shoes would start to hurt.
In 2010, scientists scanned the calves of women who'd worn heels five days a week for at least two years.
Their calf muscle fibres were about thirteen percent shorter than in women who wore flats.
Their Achilles tendons had become thicker and stiffer, too.
The body had remodeled itself around a foot that's always pointed.
So when they took the heels off, walking flat felt like a stretch. The shoes had rebuilt their legs.

description:
What if you always wore high heels? A 2010 study in the Journal of Applied Physiology compared long-term heel wearers (at least 5 cm, five days a week, two years or more) with women who wore flats.
The heel wearers' calf muscle fibres were about 13% shorter and their Achilles tendons thicker and stiffer, which can make walking in flat shoes uncomfortable.
